assessments.reasoning: json/details/NPOSL-3.0.json gives NPOSL-3.0, “Non-Profit Open Software License 3.0” and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Both crossRef and seeAlso give https://opensource.org/license/NPOSL-3.0, and licenseText contains the Non-Profit notice.
The SPDX repository’s unsigned annotated v3.29.0 object identifies target type commit and SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The NPOSL-3.0 detail comes from that exact revision.
OSI record 546 displays NPOSL-3.0 and identifies the Non-Profit edition in its title, application notice and section 17. The section 8 difference concerns wording outside the identifier claim.

challenge.method: Tested substitution of OSL-3.0 for NPOSL-3.0 against the release target, detail fields, reference route, notice and section 17. Compared section 8 with the amendment description in 17(c).
challenge.results: The ID, route and notice specify NPOSL-3.0 throughout. SPDX section 8 includes “direct” damages. OSI section 8 starts its list with “indirect,” although OSI section 17(c) says “direct” was added. That discrepancy defeats a claim of identical wording while leaving the named-edition mapping supported.

limitations: Identifier correspondence gives no verdict on equality of legal bodies, compatibility, work-specific applicability or historical approval. The OSI and SPDX renderings actually differ in section 8.
reasoning: The SPDX license detail at the v3.29.0 target assigns NPOSL-3.0 to Non-Profit Open Software License 3.0. The publisher and detail agree on the Non-Profit application notice and the separately named edition in section 17.
